results.title: Empty sum of sequents has an empty right summand
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An empty sum has an empty right residual context.

results.title: Case split on an equation of cons sequents
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Distinguish a principal selected occurrence using decidable equality. Given `a ::ₘ Γ = b ::ₘ Δ`, either `a = b` and `Γ = Δ`, or `a ≠ b` and the propositions are swapped: `Γ = b ::ₘ Λ` and `Δ = a ::ₘ Λ` for some `Λ`. The tail `Δ` can be an arbitrary multiset; the residual list is obtained from `Γ`.

results.title: Locating a head proposition in a sum of sequents
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given `a ::ₘ Γ = (Δ : Sequent) + Θ`, locate `a` in either `Δ` or `Θ` and erase it from that summand, returning the residual list.

results.title: Case split of a cons against replicated copies
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given `Multiset.replicate n a + Γ = b ::ₘ Δ`, either the head `b` is one of the `n` copies of `a` (so `b = a` and the tail is `replicate (n-1) a + Γ`), or `b` belongs to `Γ` (so `Δ = Multiset.replicate n a + Γ'` where `Γ = b ::ₘ Γ'`). The tail `Δ` can be an arbitrary multiset; the residual list is obtained from `Γ`.

results.title: Splitting replicated copies across a sum of sequents
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given `Multiset.replicate n a + Γ = (Δ : Sequent) + Θ`, split the `n` copies of `a` between `Δ` and `Θ`, returning counts `k` and `l` and residual lists.

results.title: Ordinal–cardinal Ramsey property
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For ordinals $\alpha$, $\beta$ and a cardinal $c$, the partition property $\alpha \to (\beta, c)^2$ holds if for every coloring of the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$ in red and blue, either some set of vertices whose order type is $\beta$ has all its edges red, or some set of vertices of cardinality exactly $c$ has all its edges blue.

results.title: Homogeneous set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $c$ assign a colour in $\gamma$ to each finite subset of a type $I$, and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A set $H \subseteq I$ is homogeneous for $c$ with colour $k \in \gamma$ if $c(s) = k$ for every $n$-element subset $s$ of $H$.

results.title: Partition relation for pairs with two colours
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For cardinals $\kappa$ and $\mu$, the relation $\kappa \to (\mu)^2_2$ holds if for every set $X$ of cardinality $\kappa$ and every symmetric colouring $c$ of the ordered pairs of elements of $X$ with two colours, there are a subset $H \subseteq X$ of cardinality $\mu$ and a colour $b$ such that $c(x, y) = b$ for all distinct $x, y \in H$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 591
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that, for $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$, every red/blue colouring of the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$ (that is, every pair of complementary simple graphs, red and blue, on this set) has a red clique whose order type is $\alpha$ or a blue clique with exactly $3$ elements. In partition notation, $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 591 is true
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$. For every red/blue colouring of the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$, that is, every pair of complementary simple graphs (red and blue) on this set, there is a red clique whose order type is $\alpha$ or a blue clique with exactly $3$ elements. In partition notation, $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 118 for ordinals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying the partition relation $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ and every natural number $n \ge 3$, the ordinal $\alpha$ also satisfies $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 118 fails for ordinals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist an ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying the partition relation $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ and a natural number $n \ge 3$ such that $\alpha$ does not satisfy $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$.

results.title: Quasicyclic group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $Q$ is quasicyclic if it is abelian and infinite and every proper subgroup of $Q$ is finite.

results.title: Chernikov group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is a Chernikov group if it has a normal subgroup of finite index that is isomorphic to a direct product $Q_1 \times \dots \times Q_r$ of finitely many quasicyclic groups $Q_1, \dots, Q_r$. The case $r = 0$ is allowed, so every finite group is a Chernikov group.

results.title: Groups containing the square of a quasicyclic group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ contains a direct product of two quasicyclic groups over the same prime when there are a quasicyclic group $Q$ and an injective group homomorphism $Q \times Q \to G$ (quasicyclic groups over the same prime are isomorphic).

results.title: Poset of finite order dimension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A partially ordered set has finite (order) dimension: its order relation is the intersection of finitely many linear orders on the same set.

results.title: Higman embedding theorem for Burnside varieties
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is $n_0$ such that for every odd $n \ge n_0$, every group of exponent $n$ given by generators $x_0, x_1, \dots$ and a recursively enumerable set of relators embeds in a group finitely presented in the Burnside variety $\mathfrak{B}_n$: a group with generators $x_0, \dots, x_{m-1}$ for some $m$ whose relators are a finite set $S$ together with $w^n$ for every word $w$.

results.title: Ratio of consecutive zero-based prime-indexed primes tends to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p_0 = 2$, $p_1 = 3$, $p_2 = 5$, $\dots$ be the primes in increasing order, indexed from zero, and let $q_n = p_{p_n}$. Then $q_n / q_{n+1} \to 1$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Broughan–Barnett ratio limit, zero-based form

results.title: Squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm in a family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $H$ be a real inner product space, let $T : H \to H$ be a continuous linear operator and let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $H$. The squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm of $T$ in the family $(u_n)$ is the extended nonnegative real $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \|T u_n\|^2$, the sum being taken in $[0, \infty]$. It is $\infty$ exactly when the real series $\sum_n \|T u_n\|^2$ diverges.

results.title: Extended Hilbert–Schmidt norm in a family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $H$ be a real inner product space, let $T : H \to H$ be a continuous linear operator and let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $H$. The Hilbert–Schmidt norm of $T$ in the family $(u_n)$ is the square root, taken in $[0, \infty]$ with $\sqrt{\infty} = \infty$, of the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \|T u_n\|^2 \in [0, \infty]$.

results.summary: Let $\mathbb{F}_3$ be the field with three elements. The largest subset of $\mathbb{F}_3^3$ containing no three-term arithmetic progression, that is, no elements $a, b, c$ of the subset with $a + c = 2b$ and $a \neq b$, has exactly $9$ elements.

results.title: Roth numbers from five to fourteen
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $r_3(n)$ be the largest size of a subset of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ containing no three-term arithmetic progression, that is, no elements $a, b, c$ of the subset with $a + c = 2b$ and $a \neq b$. Then the values $r_3(5), r_3(6), \dots, r_3(14)$ are $4, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 8$, in this order.

results.title: Elder's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $k \ge 1$. The total number of times the part $k$ occurs, counted with multiplicity, over all partitions of $n$ equals the sum, over all partitions $\lambda$ of $n$, of the number of distinct parts of $\lambda$ that occur at least $k$ times in $\lambda$.

results.title: Stanley's theorem

results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the total number of parts equal to $1$, counted with multiplicity, over all partitions of $n$ equals the sum, over all partitions $\lambda$ of $n$, of the number of distinct parts of $\lambda$.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $L$ of pairs of natural numbers, where the size of a pair $(k, j)$ is $k$, and a natural number $n$, this is the finite set of multisets of pairs defined by recursion on $L$. For the empty list it is the set containing only the empty multiset when $n = 0$, and the empty set otherwise. For a list with head $c$ of size $k$ and tail $L'$, it is the set of all multisets obtained by adding $i$ copies of $c$…

results.title: Membership in the multisets with a given size sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a list of pairs of natural numbers in which every pair $(k, j)$ has size $k \ge 1$, and let $n$ be a natural number. A multiset $s$ of pairs belongs to the set of multisets drawn from $L$ with size sum $n$ if and only if every element of $s$ lies in $L$ and the sizes of the elements of $s$, counted with multiplicity, sum to $n$.

results.title: n-color partitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $m$, the $n$-color partitions of $m$ form the finite set of multisets of colored parts $k_j$, that is pairs $(k, j)$ of natural numbers with $1 \le j \le k$ (a part of size $k$ comes in $k$ colors), whose sizes $k$, counted with multiplicity, sum to $m$.

results.title: Characterization of $n$-color partitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m$, a multiset $s$ of pairs of natural numbers is an $n$-color partition of $m$ if and only if every element $(k, j)$ of $s$ satisfies $1 \le j \le k$ and the sizes $k$ of the elements of $s$, counted with multiplicity, sum to $m$.

results.title: Instances of precedence-constrained multiprocessor scheduling
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance is a tuple $(d, P, m, D)$ in which $d = (d_0, \dots, d_{n-1})$ is a list of natural numbers, $d_j$ being the duration of job $j$; $P$ is a list of pairs $(a, b)$ of natural numbers, each read as the precedence constraint that job $a$ precedes job $b$; $m$ is a natural number, the number of machines; and $D$ is a natural number, the deadline.

results.title: Well-formed precedence-multiprocessor scheduling instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(d, P, m, D)$ whose list of job durations $d$ has length $n$ is well formed when every precedence pair $(a, b) \in P$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$, and there is an ordering of the jobs $0, \dots, n-1$ (a permutation of this list) in which $a$ comes before $b$ for every $(a, b) \in P$.

results.title: Feasible precedence-multiprocessor scheduling instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(d, P, m, D)$ with job durations $d = (d_0, \dots, d_{n-1})$ is feasible when there are start times $s_0, \dots, s_{n-1} \in \mathbb{N}$ and machines $\mu_0, \dots, \mu_{n-1} \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\mu_j < m$ and $s_j + d_j \le D$ for every $j < n$, $s_a + d_a \le s_b$ for every precedence pair $(a, b) \in P$, and for all jobs $a < b < n$ with $\mu_a = \mu_b$, either $s_a + d_a \le s_b$ or…

results.title: The precedence-constrained multiprocessor scheduling decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a precedence-multiprocessor scheduling instance that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.

results.title: PRECEDENCE-CONSTRAINED MULTIPROCESSOR SCHEDULING is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The precedence-constrained multiprocessor scheduling decision problem is in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
